headline: AI's leaders wobble as agents start spending your money
summary: The week's power shifted twice: at the top of the AI industry, and at the checkout. Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO effective immediately, and Anthropic filed to go public, so your chip supplier and a key model vendor now face new scrutiny. Meanwhile agents became customers: a16z says agent web traffic grew 8x from August to October, Muse now places phone calls for users, and Replit Agent can buy ads. Some gatekeepers are pushing back, with United refusing bookings from unauthorized agents. Inside companies, Claude moved into video calls, and Anthropic now lets you host its agents in your own cloud. This quarter, decide which agents may spend or speak for your company, and which outside agents you will let in.

threads.title: Agents with a wallet

threads.title: The bouncer at the door

threads.title: The assistant is the office

threads.title: Speed beats size
threads.line: Google's fast Hydrogen came a day after Theo timed Carbon as slow. Quick, cheap models take more daily work; retest defaults.
